title: [CQ-R13d] Native isolation certify command
definitionOfDone: The injected core produces a report of the exact schema with transport 'injected' and certified false, even when every check passes. Only a native run whose every registry check passed certifies. Shown by tests.

Checks run in registry order, and a failed check leaves every later check 'not-run' except teardown. Teardown always deletes exactly this run's VM and leaves no live ledger record of its attempt. Shown by tests with a fake provider.
validateCertificationReport accepts exactly the schema with the current check ids, and refuses anything else with CERTIFY_REPORT_INVALID. Shown by tests.

`cli.mjs certify` refuses any argument shape but `--work-dir <absolute path>` and refuses an unsupported host with a fixed code. It writes its report O_EXCL with mode 0600 and exits 0 only when certified. Shown by tests.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

CQ-R13a (task-6dd3ce1f) lands first: it changes cli.mjs argument parsing for --cache-dir and adds its rows. Re-read cli.mjs, native-smoke.mjs and the native-smoke section of scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs (~2482-2690) before editing.

In scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs, after the native-smoke rows, reuse smokeHarness's fake provider, image download and delete recorder, plus assertSanitized and scratch. Rows CF1-CF8 call the injected core, certifyCore({ platform, workDir, deps }):
- CF1: with every check passing, the report has exactly the schema:
  - {kind:'isolation-certification', version:1, platform, arch, transport:'injected', provider:{name:'multipass', version}, image:{sourceSha256, providerImageHash}, supervisorSha256, startedAt, finishedAt, checks, certified:false, executionReady:false};
  - checks are exactly CERTIFY_CHECKS' ids in order, each {id, result:'passed', code:null};
  - injected evidence never certifies.
- CF2: a readiness failure gives provision 'passed', then readiness 'failed' with readiness's own fixed failure code, no-mounts 'not-run' and teardown 'passed'.
  - Teardown deleted exactly this run's VM (the delete recorder).
  - The ledger keeps no live record of this run's attempt.
  - A foreign record seeded in the same ledger survives.
- CF3:
  - A provision rejection: that check fails with its fixed code, every later check except teardown is 'not-run', and teardown passes with nothing reserved.
  - A check whose run throws an unexpected error fails with CERTIFY_CHECK_FAILED, and teardown still runs.
  - certifyCore never rejects after input validation.
- CF4: the JSON report never contains the credential bytes (hex or base64), the workDir path or any host path, and every code matches /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/.
- CF5: validateCertificationReport.
  - It returns a frozen copy of a well-formed native report.
  - It refuses with CERTIFY_REPORT_INVALID: a missing or extra key at any depth; a wrong kind or version; missing, extra or reordered check ids; a result outside the enum; a non-null, non-code code; certified that differs from (transport === 'native' && every check passed); executionReady true; and a non-ISO timestamp.
- CF6: runIsolationCertify, the native entry, refuses every shape but exactly { workDir: <absolute, no control characters> } with CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID, mirroring the smoke's options list. With process.platform overridden to 'sunos', as the smoke's row does, it refuses with CERTIFY_UNSUPPORTED_HOST. Neither creates workDir.
- CF7: the core writes the report to <workDir>/certification-<platform>-<arch>-<UTC stamp>-<random>.json, opened 'wx' with mode 0600, asserted on POSIX only. The file's bytes equal JSON of the returned report.
- CF8: through runCli:
  - `certify --work-dir <abs>` calls the injected certify and exits 0 only when certified === true;
  - every other shape (a missing or relative path, an extra flag) is CLI_INPUT_INVALID with exit 2;
  - a CERTIFY_* rejection prints {code, certified:false, executionReady:false} and exits 2.

In scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs, `required` gains 'certify.mjs'.

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs`. The new rows fail, and every other row passes.

Error handling in the tests: assertions name fixed codes, never messages, and every scratch directory is removed in t.after.

Deviations, intent kept:

- CF3 also covers blocked prerequisites (CERTIFY_PROVISION_UNAVAILABLE), retry exhaustion after a reserve (teardown settles the record with no delete) and a failed delete (CERTIFY_TEARDOWN_FAILED).

amendments.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

CQ-R13a (task-6dd3ce1f) lands first. It changes cli.mjs argument parsing (--cache-dir) and adds its own rows. Before editing, re-read cli.mjs, native-smoke.mjs and the native-smoke section of scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs (~2482-2690).

THE HARNESS. In scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs, after the native-smoke rows, add certifyHarness. It is smokeHarness (line ~2602) with two differences:
- The fake VM answers healthy({ supervisorHash: <the SMOKE_SUPERVISOR shape built from the sha256 of the REAL scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py bytes>, ...guest }).
- deps is { provider: { run }, fetch, digest: pinDigest().digest, sleep, random: sequence(), doctor: async () => ({ providerReady: true, version: '1.17.0' }), now: () => new Date('2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z') }.
Reuse its delete recorder, scratch() and assertSanitized (for thrown errors).

Rows CF1-CF7 call the injected core certifyCore({ platform, workDir, deps }):

- CF1, all pass. deepStrictEqual against an exact literal: {kind:'isolation-certification', version:1, platform, arch, transport:'injected', provider:{name:'multipass', version:'1.17.0'}, image:{sourceSha256, providerImageHash}, supervisorSha256, startedAt:'2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z', finishedAt:'2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z', checks, certified:false, executionReady:false}.
  - checks are exactly CERTIFY_CHECKS' ids in order, each {id, result:'passed', code:null}, and teardown is last.
  - supervisorSha256 is the sha256 of the real guest-supervisor.py bytes.
  - Injected evidence never certifies.

- CF2, readiness fails.
  - provision is 'passed', readiness 'failed' with the readiness failure's own code, no-mounts {result:'not-run', code:null}, and teardown 'passed'.
  - The delete recorder shows exactly this run's VM deleted.
  - ledger.read(<captured name>).phase is 'deleted'.
  - A foreign record seeded in the same ledger (random () => Buffer.alloc(10, 0xab)) survives, still Running.

- CF3, rejections.
  - A provision rejection fails 'provision' with its own code. Every later BODY check is 'not-run'. Teardown passes with nothing reserved and no delete.
  - A check whose run throws a codeless error fails with CERTIFY_CHECK_FAILED, and teardown still runs. Inject this by making the fake no-mounts probe throw.
  - certifyCore never rejects after input validation, except CF7's write failure.

- CF4, no leak. The report's JSON never contains the workDir, tmpdir() or any absolute path, and every non-null code matches /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/. CF1's exact-literal equality is what proves that no credential or guest byte can reach it.

- CF5, validateCertificationReport.
  - It returns a frozen copy of a well-formed native report (transport 'native', certified true, every check passed).
  - Every refusal is CERTIFY_REPORT_INVALID, via assertSanitized. Refuse:
    - a missing or extra key at any depth;
    - a wrong kind or version;
    - missing, extra or reordered check ids;
    - a result outside passed/failed/not-run;
    - a code that is neither null nor a stable code;
    - certified !== (transport === 'native' && every check passed), in both directions;
    - executionReady true;
    - a non-ISO timestamp.

- CF6, the native entry runIsolationCertify.
  - Every options shape except exactly { workDir: <absolute, control-free> } is CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID. Mirror the smoke's list: undefined, null, an array, an extra key, a symbol key, a relative path, a control character.
  - With process.platform redefined to 'sunos', it is CERTIFY_UNSUPPORTED_HOST. Restore process.platform in a finally, as the smoke row does.
  - Neither refusal creates workDir.
  - certifyCore with a relative workDir, or with a non-record platform, is CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID before any provider call (the fake records no call).

- CF7, the report file.
  - The core writes <workDir>/certification-<platform>-<arch>-20260102T030405Z-<6 hex>.json. Find it with readdirSync. Its bytes JSON.parse to the returned report (deepStrictEqual).
  - On POSIX only, statSync(file).mode & 0o777 === 0o600.
  - Then, in a FRESH workDir, use a fixed random (size => Buffer.alloc(size, 0x11)), so the name ends -111111.json, and pre-create that exact file with known bytes. The core rejects CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED (assertSanitized). The pre-existing bytes are unchanged, because 'wx' never overwrites. The delete recorder shows teardown already deleted the VM.

- CF8, through runCli.
  - `certify --work-dir <abs>` calls the injected certify with exactly { workDir }. It exits 0 only when certified === true; a certified:false report exits 2.
  - A missing --work-dir, a relative path or an extra flag is CLI_INPUT_INVALID with exit 2.
  - A CERTIFY_* rejection prints {code, certified:false, executionReady:false} and exits 2.
  - Any other rejection prints code CERTIFY_UNAVAILABLE.

THE BUNDLE TEST. In scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs, `required` gains 'certify.mjs'.

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs`. The new rows fail and every other row passes.

ERROR HANDLING in the tests: assert fixed codes, never messages. Remove every scratch directory in t.after.
amendments.reason: These changes align the rows with step 2's settled write-failure contract. CF3's 'never rejects' now excepts the report write, and CF7 proves 'wx' exclusivity plus teardown-before-write. The harness now uses the real supervisor hash and injected doctor/now. CF4 relies on CF1's exact-literal equality rather than credential capture.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/local-runner/certify.mjs, modeled on native-smoke.mjs. Its header states:
- it is operator-invoked on real hardware, never in CI;
- it is the only evidence that can establish an isolation support claim;
- certification is not activation: executionReady stays false and verified-local stays unavailable.

Registry:
- CERTIFY_CHECKS = Object.freeze([...BODY, TEARDOWN]), each entry a frozen {id, run(context)}. run resolves {result: 'passed'|'failed', code}.
- BODY is 'provision', 'readiness', 'no-mounts'. CQ-R13e/f/h/g append to BODY, so 'teardown' always stays last.

The checks:
- 'provision': provisionGuest({ platform, ledger, owner, cacheDir: <workDir>/images, supervisor, credential, provider }).
  - It uses an observed platform whose prerequisites capture the detected arch, exactly as native-smoke does.
  - It uses a ledger wrapper whose reserve captures this run's instance name, as check-lifecycle.mjs does.
  - supervisor is the REAL bytes of ./guest-supervisor.py, read through new URL(..., import.meta.url). credential is randomBytes(32).
  - It passes only when provisioned === true and instance equals the captured name.
- 'readiness': passes only when bootstrapReady === true and failures is an empty array. Otherwise it fails with failures[0] (readiness's own fixed codes, which name a degraded cloud-init boot) or CERTIFY_NOT_READY.
- 'no-mounts': assertNoMounts(name, provider); a refusal fails with its TRANSFER_* code.
- 'teardown': always runs.
  - With no captured name, it passes.
  - Otherwise deleteOwned({ ledger, name, owner, provider }) must resolve 'deleted' or 'not-launched', and ledger.read(name) must show no live record of this attempt. Anything else fails with CERTIFY_TEARDOWN_FAILED.

Runner, run(platform, workDir, deps, native):
- The owner is synthetic: { taskId: 'task-certify', attemptId: 'attempt-' + 32 random hex, generation: 1 }.
- The ledger is createLedger(<workDir>/ledger, { random: deps.random }).
- Checks run in order. After the first failure, every BODY check is 'not-run'.
- Each run is wrapped. A throw becomes 'failed' with the error's code when it matches /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/, else CERTIFY_CHECK_FAILED.
- provider.version comes from runDoctor({ executable })'s version when providerReady, else null. The report has no executable path, because it carries no host path.
- certified = native && every check passed.
- The report is deep-frozen. It is written to <workDir>/certification-<platform>-<arch>-<UTC stamp>-<6 hex>.json, where the stamp is YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ with no ':' (Windows-safe). The file is opened with fs.promises.open(path, 'wx', 0o600), then written, synced and closed.
- A write failure returns the report with certified false, and a failed 'teardown'-independent code CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED recorded as the last check's code. Hmm: keep it simple, and instead throw CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED after teardown has run.

Exports:
- certifyCore({ platform, workDir, deps }): injected, never certifies.
- runIsolationCertify(options): the native entry. options must be exactly { workDir } (absolute, with no control characters, and its own keys checked by Reflect.ownKeys), else CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID. platformFor(process.platform) null gives CERTIFY_UNSUPPORTED_HOST. Neither refusal creates workDir.
- validateCertificationReport(value).
- CERTIFY_CHECKS.

Error handling: fixed codes only, with a MESSAGES table of fixed text and no path or byte. Teardown runs on every path after provisioning has started.
implementationPlan.note:
Created scripts/local-runner/certify.mjs (~190 lines) per amend-1, reusing native-smoke's owner, observed-platform and provider-executable patterns and check-lifecycle's capturing ledger.

- CERTIFY_CHECKS is frozen: provision, readiness, no-mounts, teardown.
- runCheck maps a throw to its stable code, else CERTIFY_CHECK_FAILED.
- Teardown uses deleteOwned by exact name; any rejection is CERTIFY_TEARDOWN_FAILED.
- The report is deep-frozen and written 'wx' 0600 to certification-<platform>-<arch|unknown>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<6hex>.json. mkdir is recursive with mode 0700. A write failure rejects CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED after teardown, removing only a partial file this run opened.
- validateCertificationReport does exact keys at every depth (Reflect.ownKeys, plain prototype, each value read once). It requires the current ids in order, result/code consistency and not-run only after a body failure, and teardown never not-run. It requires certified === (native && all passed) and executionReady false, and returns a deep-frozen copy.

Hardening beyond the plan text:
- certifyCore requires platform.id to be in win32/linux/darwin, not just any string, because the id goes into the report file name (path safety).
- The report arch is IMAGE_ARCHES-only, else null.
- The version must match /^[0-9A-Za-z.+-]{1,64}$/.
- now() falls back to the real clock when its value is not ISO.

CF1-CF7 pass. CF8 and the USAGE rows wait for step 3.

amendments.description:
Create scripts/local-runner/certify.mjs, modeled on native-smoke.mjs. Reuse its owner, observed-platform and provider-executable patterns verbatim.

The header states:
- it is operator-invoked on real hardware, never CI;
- it is the only evidence that can establish an isolation support claim;
- certification is not activation: executionReady stays false and verified-local stays unavailable.

REGISTRY: CERTIFY_CHECKS = Object.freeze([...BODY, TEARDOWN]). Each entry is a frozen {id, run(context)}, and run resolves {result: 'passed'|'failed', code}. BODY holds 'provision', 'readiness' and 'no-mounts'. CQ-R13e/f/h/g append to BODY only, so 'teardown' is always last.

CHECKS:
- 'provision' reads SUPERVISOR = the REAL bytes of ./guest-supervisor.py, via readFile(new URL('./guest-supervisor.py', import.meta.url)). A read failure fails with CERTIFY_SUPERVISOR_UNAVAILABLE. It then calls provisionGuest({ platform: observed, ledger: capturing, owner, cacheDir: path.join(workDir, 'images'), supervisor: SUPERVISOR, credential: randomBytes(32), provider, fetch: deps.fetch, digest: deps.digest, sleep: deps.sleep }).
  - observed wraps platform.prerequisites to capture the detected arch, exactly as native-smoke does.
  - capturing is check-lifecycle.mjs's ledger wrapper. Its reserve records this run's instance name on the context, even when provisioning later throws.
  - provider = { ...deps.provider, executable: deps.provider?.executable ?? platform.executable }.
  - It passes only when outcome.provisioned === true and outcome.instance equals the captured name. The outcome is kept on the context.
  - provisioned !== true fails with CERTIFY_PROVISION_UNAVAILABLE. An instance mismatch fails with CERTIFY_PROVISION_FAILED.
- 'readiness' passes only when bootstrapReady === true and failures is an empty array. Otherwise it fails with failures[0] when that is a stable code (readiness's own fixed codes, a degraded cloud-init boot among them), else with CERTIFY_NOT_READY.
- 'no-mounts' calls assertNoMounts(name, provider) from snapshot-transfer.mjs. A refusal fails with its TRANSFER_* code.
- 'teardown' always runs, whatever happened before.
  - With no captured name, it passes.
  - Otherwise deleteOwned({ ledger, name, owner, provider }) must resolve 'deleted' or 'not-launched'. Anything else, a rejection included, fails with CERTIFY_TEARDOWN_FAILED.
  - It deletes by exact owned name, so a foreign record in the same ledger is never touched.

RUNNER: run(platform, workDir, deps, native).
- owner = { taskId: 'task-certify', attemptId: `attempt-${randomBytes(16).toString('hex')}`, generation: 1 }.
- ledger = createLedger(path.join(workDir, 'ledger'), { random: deps.random }).
- Checks run in order. After the first failed BODY check, every remaining BODY check is recorded {result: 'not-run', code: null}, and teardown still runs.
- Every run call is wrapped. A throw becomes 'failed' with the error's code when it matches /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/, else CERTIFY_CHECK_FAILED. No check can reject the run.
- provider.version comes from (deps.doctor ?? runDoctor)({ executable: provider.executable }): its version when providerReady === true, else null, and a throw also gives null. The report never carries the executable or any other host path.
- certified = native && every check passed. executionReady is always false.
- startedAt and finishedAt are (deps.now ?? (() => new Date()))().toISOString().
- After teardown, the report is deep-frozen and written to path.join(workDir, `certification-${platform.id}-${arch}-${stamp}-${hex}.json`).
  - stamp is startedAt as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ, with no ':' so the name is Windows-safe.
  - hex is (deps.random ?? randomBytes)(3) as 6 hex characters.
  - The file is opened with fs.promises.open(file, 'wx', 0o600), written, synced, and closed in a finally.
- Any write failure rejects CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED. That includes an existing file, because 'wx' never overwrites. Teardown has already run by then. This is the ONLY rejection after input validation.

EXPORTS:
- certifyCore({ platform, workDir, deps = {} }) takes the injected transports {provider, fetch, digest, sleep, random, doctor, now}. Its transport is 'injected', so it never certifies. Before any call, it refuses with CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID when workDir is not an absolute, control-free string, or when platform is not a record with a string id and a prerequisites function.
- runIsolationCertify(options) is the native entry. options must be exactly { workDir } (Reflect.ownKeys yields the single key 'workDir'; the path is absolute and has no control characters), else CERTIFY_INPUT_INVALID. A null platformFor(process.platform) gives CERTIFY_UNSUPPORTED_HOST. Neither refusal creates workDir. It runs with deps {} and native true.
- validateCertificationReport(value) returns a deep-frozen copy, or throws CERTIFY_REPORT_INVALID.
- CERTIFY_CHECKS.

ERROR HANDLING: fixed codes only. A MESSAGES table holds fixed text that never carries a path, credential byte or guest byte. Errors are thrown as Object.assign(new Error(MESSAGES[code]), { code }), as native-smoke does. Teardown runs on every path once provisioning has started.
amendments.reason: The submitted text left two write-failure contracts side by side. One is settled now: the run rejects CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED after teardown. implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review done. Fixed one finding: validateCertificationReport used to accept a certified:true report with arch null or a null image/supervisor hash, which is unevidenced certification. A null arch or hash is now valid only when certified is false. Added CF5 rows certifiedNoArch and certifiedNoHash, and confirmed they fail with the old guard (red), then restored. Concurrency: two runs sharing a workDir cannot collide. The ledger reserves 'wx' under a random 80-bit VM name, and the report is 'wx' with a random 6-hex suffix, so a collision is CERTIFY_REPORT_WRITE_FAILED and never an overwrite. Teardown always runs and deletes only the exact owned name. Error paths: the report handle closes in a finally, and only a file this run opened is unlinked. Theoretical only: runCheck reads error?.code from an error thrown inside our own modules, so a hostile throwing getter could reject; that is not reachable from external input. Fresh verification: exit 0, 315 tests, 314 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip; git diff --check is clean. Net change is 387 added / 12 removed, under the 400 cap.

completionSummary:
CQ-R13d native isolation certify command.

New file scripts/local-runner/certify.mjs:
- CERTIFY_CHECKS runs in a fixed order: provision, readiness, no-mounts, teardown.
- Provision uses the real guest-supervisor.py hash, with an owned ledger and a synthetic owner.
- Readiness requires cloud-init done/done; a degraded boot gives BOOTSTRAP_FAILED.
- No-mounts uses assertNoMounts.
- Teardown always runs and deletes only this run's exact owned VM, through deleteOwned.
- After a failure, the remaining body checks are 'not-run'.
- certifyCore (injectable) always gives transport 'injected' and certified false. runIsolationCertify (native) accepts exactly {workDir}, refuses an unsupported host with CERTIFY_UNSUPPORTED_HOST, and certifies only when every check passed.
- executionReady is always false.
- The report holds fixed codes and hashes only: no paths, no secrets. It is written to certification-<platform>-<arch>-<stamp>-<6hex>.json with 'wx' and mode 0600, never overwriting.
- validateCertificationReport checks exact keys at every depth, check order and not-run order, result/code consistency, and that certified matches (native && all passed). It refuses a certified report that is missing its arch or a hash. Anything else throws CERTIFY_REPORT_INVALID.
